plain.text: It was two days before the Passover. The chief priests and teachers of the law were looking for a sly way to arrest and kill Jesus, but not during the festival, in case the people rioted.

In Bethany, at the home of Simon the leper, a woman came with a jar of very expensive perfume. She broke the jar and poured it on Jesus' head. Some were angry: "Why waste it? It could have been sold and the money given to the poor!" Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She has done a beautiful thing for me. You will always have the poor, but you will not always have me. She anointed my body beforehand for burial. Wherever the good news is preached, what she has done will be told in memory of her."
Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus. They were delighted and promised him money. So he watched for a chance to hand him over.

On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was sacrificed, the disciples asked where to prepare the meal. Jesus sent two of them into the city. A man carrying a jar of water would lead them to a house with a large upper room. They found everything as Jesus had said and prepared the Passover.

That evening, while they were eating, Jesus said, "One of you will betray me." They were saddened and asked, "Surely not I?" He said it was one who dipped bread into the bowl with him. While they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them, saying, "Take it; this is my body." Then he took a cup, gave thanks and they all drank from it. He said, "This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many." He said he would not drink wine again until he drank it new in God's kingdom. After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

Jesus told them, "You will all fall away." But after he had risen, he would go ahead of them to Galilee. Peter said, "Even if all fall away, I will not." Jesus said, "Today, this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times." Peter insisted he would die rather than deny him, and the others said the same.

At a place called Gethsemane, Jesus took Peter, James and John further on. He was deeply distressed and said, "My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch." He fell to the ground and prayed, "Abba, Father, everything is possible for you. Take this cup from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will." He came back and found the disciples asleep. Three times this happened. Then he said, "The hour has come. Look, my betrayer is here!"

Judas arrived with a crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent by the leaders. He had arranged a signal: "The one I kiss is the man." He kissed Jesus, and they arrested him. One of those standing near drew a sword and cut off the ear of the high priest's servant. Jesus said, "Am I leading a rebellion, that you come with swords? Every day I was teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But the Scriptures must be fulfilled." Then everyone left him and ran away. A young man following Jesus, wearing only a linen cloth, ran off naked when they grabbed him.

They took Jesus to the high priest, where the leaders gathered. Peter followed at a distance into the courtyard. Many gave false testimony, but their stories did not agree. The high priest asked, "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?" Jesus said, "I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Mighty One and coming on the clouds of heaven." The high priest tore his clothes and said, "You have heard the blasphemy!" They all condemned him as deserving death. Some spat on him, blindfolded him, struck him and mocked him.

Down in the courtyard, a servant girl saw Peter and said, "You were with Jesus." Peter denied it. Later she told others, "This man is one of them," and again he denied it. Then those standing by said, "Surely you are one of them, for you are a Galilean." Peter began to curse and swear, "I don't know this man!" Immediately the rooster crowed the second time. Peter remembered Jesus' words, broke down and wept.

summary.bigIdea: On the night before he dies, Jesus gives his disciples the bread and cup, prays in anguish, and is betrayed, deserted and condemned.
points: A woman anoints Jesus with costly perfume; he says it prepares him for burial.
At the Last Supper Jesus says, "This is my body" and "This is my blood of the covenant."
In Gethsemane Jesus prays, "Not what I will, but what you will," before being arrested.
Peter denies knowing Jesus three times, then weeps.
summary.reflection: Jesus prayed honestly in his distress, yet trusted his Father. What would it mean to pray like that in your own hard times?
